Summary first:  
- Azure errors = wrong model identifier for Azure OpenAI — you must send the Azure deployment name (the deployment id), not a provider-prefixed string.  
- Anthropic errors = wrong model string format — the request reached Anthropic with no valid "model" parameter because the configured model used a provider-prefixed value. Use the plain Anthropic model id.  
- Groq errors = max_tokens exceeds the model context window — lower max_tokens to the model’s supported context length.

1) Diagnose each error

Error Type 1 — Azure models (azure-gpt4, azure-gpt4-mini)
- Root cause: The litellm_params.model values include a provider prefix ("azure/gpt-4" etc.) rather than the Azure deployment name (the deployment ID you created in the Azure OpenAI resource). Azure OpenAI APIs expect requests targeted to a specific deployment id.
- Why this error: Azure returns 404 DeploymentNotFound because the OpenAI-compatible endpoint looks for the deployment id in the path (and/or request), and the provided model value didn't match any existing deployment. In short: the model identifier sent to Azure was incorrect.

Error Type 2 — Anthropic models (claude-opus, claude-sonnet)
- Root cause: The configured model strings include a registry prefix ("anthropic/claude-...") instead of the plain model id that Anthropic expects. LiteLLM/provider adapter ended up sending no valid "model" field to Anthropic (or the wrong shape), causing the API to complain "model: field required".
- Why this error: Anthropic's API requires a "model" parameter with the provider's model id (for example "claude-opus-4-20250514"). Using a prefixed form prevented the adapter from producing the expected "model" field in the request body.

Error Type 3 — Groq models (llama-fast, llama-mini)
- Root cause: max_tokens is set to 32768 while the Groq model’s context window is 8192 (per the error). The config requests more tokens than the model supports.
- Why this error: The Groq API validates the requested max_tokens against the model’s context length and returns 400 when you request more tokens than allowed.

2) Fixed config — only changed lines

Group B — Azure OpenAI (replace model with your actual Azure deployment id)
- For azure-gpt4:
  model: gpt-4                   # use the Azure deployment name (replace with your deployment id)
- For azure-gpt4-mini:
  model: gpt-4o-mini             # use the Azure deployment name (replace with your deployment id)

(If your Azure deployments are named e.g. "gpt4-deploy" and "gpt4o-mini-deploy", use those exact names. The key point: do NOT use "azure/..." prefix — use the deployment id.)

Group C — Anthropic
- For claude-opus:
  model: claude-opus-4-20250514
- For claude-sonnet:
  model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514

(Replace with the canonical Anthropic model ids you have access to — do not prefix with "anthropic/".)

Group E — Groq
- For llama-fast:
  max_tokens: 8192
- For llama-mini:
  max_tokens: 8192

(Adjust to the correct context window for the exact Groq model if different; set max_tokens <= the model’s context window.)

3) Validation checklist — commands / checks to verify fixes

General quick checks
- YAML lint and syntax:
  - yamllint litellm_config.yaml

- Confirm environment variables present:
  - echo "$OPENAI_API_KEY" (and other API keys) or run: env | grep -E 'OPENAI|AZURE_OPENAI|ANTHROPIC|GROQ|MISTRAL|LITELLM'

Azure-specific
- Verify deployment exists in Azure before calling LiteLLM:
  - Azure CLI (example):
    az openai deployment list --resource-name <your-resource-name> --api-version 2024-02-15-preview
    (or check in Azure Portal → OpenAI → Deployments)
- Smoke test via LiteLLM (assuming LiteLLM proxy runs at localhost:8080 and exposes a completion endpoint):
  - curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"azure-gpt4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}' | jq .
  - Expect a 200 and a valid completion (no 404 DeploymentNotFound).
- Direct Azure API minimal test (replace {deployment} and resource host):
  - curl -s -X POST "https://contoso.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/{deployment}/chat/completions?api-version=2024-02-15-preview" \
    -H "api-key: $AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":1}' | jq .

Anthropic-specific
- Minimal direct Anthropic test:
  - curl -s -X POST "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/complete" \
    -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"claude-opus-4-20250514","prompt":"Human: Hello\nAssistant:","max_tokens_to_sample":10}' | jq .
  - Expect a 200 and no "model: field required" error.
- LiteLLM smoke test:
  - curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"claude-opus","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}' | jq .
  - Expect normal response, no 400.

Groq-specific
- Confirm model context window (from Groq docs or query model metadata if available).
- LiteLLM smoke test with smaller tokens:
  - curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"llama-fast","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],"max_tokens":32}' | jq .
  - Expect 200. Then test a high but valid max_tokens close to context window (e.g., 8192) to verify behavior.
- If direct Groq API access is available, submit a minimal completion showing the model accepts <=8192 tokens.

Logging and health
- Tail LiteLLM logs during the smoke tests (journalctl / docker logs / service logs) and confirm no the earlier errors reappear.
- Check HTTP statuses: 200 OK, not 4xx/5xx for successful tests.

4) Prevention — config validation / CI checks to catch each error before deployment

Azure DeploymentNotFound prevention
- CI check: if api_base looks like an Azure host (openai.azure.com), validate model value is a plausible Azure deployment id (no provider prefix). Optionally call Azure management API (or OpenAI-compatible deployment endpoint) with the provided API key to confirm the named deployment exists. Fail the pipeline if the deployment is missing.
- Lint rule: forbid "azure/" prefix in model field when api_base contains "azure".

Anthropic model field required prevention
- CI check: require model strings for Anthropic entries to match regex for canonical model ids (e.g., ^claude[-_A-Za-z0-9]+). Reject strings that start with "anthropic/".
- Dry-run test: adapter-level validation that constructs the provider request and asserts required fields (model) are present before deploying. Unit test that builds the outgoing payload for each provider.

Groq max_tokens prevention
- Maintain a small mapping in CI/lint of known model context windows (e.g., groq/llama-3.3-70b => 8192) and validate max_tokens <= context window. If unknown model, at least warn and require a manual confirmation step.
- Add a pre-deploy smoke test that requests metadata or a minimal completion with the configured max_tokens and fails if provider responds with a context-window error.

Additional general controls
- Add a schema validator (JSON Schema/YAML schema) for litellm_config.yaml with provider-specific rules and cross-field validation (e.g., if api_base contains "openai.azure", require api_version and require model format).
- Add integration smoke-tests in CI that run minimal completion requests against a test account (or use recorded/replayed responses) for each provider group.
- Add environment variable presence checks and secrets scanning in CI.

If you want, I can:
- Produce an automated pre-deploy validation script (Python/bash) that checks for these specific errors (Azure deployment existence, Anthropic model format, Groq token limits), or
- Show exact CLI/cURL commands tailored to your LiteLLM service path and your real deployment names.
